activity_context.topic_title: The Intersection Between a Line and a Plane

feedback.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{1}=\frac{z-1}{3},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩=19.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(1,-2,1)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨2,1,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨1,-2,1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+2t,-2+t,1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨1,6,2⟩ & =19 \\ (1+2t)+6(-2+t)+2(1+3t) & =19 \\ 1+2t-12+6t+2+6t & =19 \\ 14t & =28 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨1+2(2),-2+2,1+3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,0,7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(5,0,7).$
